team: CARRICK: “GETTING CONFUSED WITH WHAT’S GOING ON!”  Sunderland
speaker: Head Coach
quote_text:
Alright? Michael, what was your assessment of  that one? Yeah, it was a tough game. Credit to  
Sunderland. I think we knew it was going to be a  tough game coming here anyway, and we had to dig  
deep at times. It wasn't our best, but actually  to take something from the game when you're not  
at your best is a good trait that we're trying to  build as well. So there were obviously changes,  
and sometimes you're trying to find that rhythm  a little bit, which is understandable, but  
I still quite liked a lot of things, you  know, to give us the foundation to then be  
able to play better at certain times. But to take  a point and a clean sheet for what it is, I think  
is okay. Michael, how do you think Josh performed?  First start since December. Yeah, to be honest,  
I thought for all the boys, it was just a tough  game. It was an away game coming here, which is  
challenging, you know, and I thought there were  certain times when Josh linked the play really  
well and certain times when we probably left him  a little bit isolated at times, and that's how  
it goes. I think he played a real part for the  team and I understand it's not always easy for  
any player when you haven't played for a little  bit to come into a game. So certainly not just  
judging any individual on just one performance  today anyway. Michael, that felt maybe like  
something next season's going to look like, and  there's going to be a lot more games and you have  
to do a lot more rotation. Did it feel like a  sign that maybe you're going to need more depth  
this summer and more options when you do pick up  those little injuries? It's one game as well. I  
think to overanalyse it in terms of then moving  forward next season, judging the squad and judging  
everything on one game, it's certainly not what  I'll do or what we'll do as a club anyway. I think  
we know the quality of the players, we know what  the squad looks like and the strengths and things  
that we need to improve on. So certainly one game  today doesn't change our minds in any of that.  
Michael, normally at this point in the season  there's an accusation that certain teams are on  
the beach. Do you feel you need to guard against  any complacency in your team, having achieved  
Champions League qualification? No, I almost get  offended by that when people are accusing that,  
because the way the players have prepared for  the game, the way they left the changing room,  
we faced a tough game. It's fine. I think if  we weren't in a good headspace and motivated,  
I think we lose the game today. Sunderland played  really well at certain points of the game and made  
us work for it. So I think the fact that our pride  in ourselves and each other and the responsibility  
of playing for this great club and being part  of it, certainly motivation and focus is not  
the reason whether we're going to be brilliant or  maybe going to have a performance where it comes a  
little bit more challenging. Whether it's today  or the next two games, that won't be the case,  
whether that's affected at all. Can I ask about  the injury status of Casemiro and Sesko as well?  
Yeah, we'll just have to see the boys. Casemiro  will be fine. It's not a major issue. He'll be  
fine next week. Ben, we'll just have to see. He's  been carrying a shin problem for a little bit of  
time now, so we've just got to manage that and see  what's best for him. Casemiro, obviously people  
have spoken a lot about him leaving at the end  of the season. Is this a chance for you to assess  
what you have and what those players can give you  in that position? Because clearly it's a crucial  
part of the pitch and we expect that's where the  club's going to be looking in the summer. Yeah,  
not just totally on one game or two games. I  don't think the whole assessment of a direction  
of where we need to go will be judged on that. I  think over time you get a clear picture of what  
it looks like. Some positives, some negatives,  what we need to improve on. So certainly today,  
next week and the week after, that's not going to  be a total decisive factor in making decisions. It  
needs a bit more laying of foundations to make  decisions than just one or two games. Michael,  
you've recently been speaking about red cards and  violent conduct. Obviously Lisandro Martinez is  
one. Were you surprised it wasn't a red card  at the end of today's game? To be honest,  
I genuinely haven't seen it on TV. Bruno said  there was contact and he wasn't too happy about  
it when he came in. The staff on the bench weren't  too happy with it as well. So yeah, I don't know.  
Getting a little bit confused with some of what's  going on, really, so I'm better off staying out of  
it. Mr Carrick, you've come up to the North East  twice this year, and it seems like the United team  
has struggled quite a little bit. Do you feel  like it's the atmosphere that North East fans,  
you know, you'll be familiar with, that generates  that, that means the United players struggle when  
they come up here? I don't think we struggle.  I don't. I think the boys are used to playing  
in all sorts of different atmospheres. I  think it's just two separate occasions,  
two good teams, different games. You know,  it's part of it. I think we've played away in  
other games and won and had good results in  different types of atmospheres. So, I mean,  
you just take each game separately, really. Thank  you. Thanks. All right, guys. Cheers. Thanks.
title: CARRICK: “GETTING CONFUSED WITH WHAT’S GOING ON!”  Sunderland 0-0 Man Utd
